result.title: DISTRACT: Degradation-Indexed Study of Textual Reference Across Competing Targets
result.summary: Vision-language trackers (VLTs) accept descriptions intended to assist tracking, but accepting text does not establish that its content changes tracking decisions, particularly as visual evidence deteriorates. We introduce DISTRACT, a matched-intervention benchmark that holds video, target, and distractor fixed while crossing four text priors with four image degradations along a controlled severity axis. We evaluate five VLTs on four datasets using behavioral contrasts, layerwise representation probes, and activation patching. Molmo2 and JointNLT exhibit directed text use. Some effects contract under degradation, whereas others show no significant endpoint change after multiplicity correction. UVLTrack, MMTrack, and DUTrack respond only weakly to changes in text semantics, with no directed behavioral effect surviving FDR correction in the tested settings. Model-internal analyses reveal that at decision-near states, correct-versus-conflicting text is decodable in Molmo2 and JointNLT but not in the other three systems. In the responsive models, decodability peaks at late states where replacement produces little behavioral change, whereas replacing selected earlier states redirects conflict-associated trajectories toward the target. Because matched-correct donors do not significantly outperform unrelated donors, these interventions identify earlier intervention-sensitive states without establishing target-specific semantic rescue. DISTRACT thus exposes when and where text affects tracking under degraded visual evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DISTRACT 匹配干预基准：固定视频、目标与干扰项，交叉四种文本先验与四级图像退化，并用行为对比、逐层表征探针和激活替换评估五个视觉语言跟踪器是否真正依据文本语义作出决策。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及「模型是否真正使用多模态证据」的因果诊断：退化轴加 activation patching 可供核查决策邻近状态的可解码性是否等于因果贡献、以及视觉证据恶化时文本旁路的作用；但任务为跟踪而非 latent 推理生成，迁移性需核查。
